rpo.note: Backlog is now massive and gives unusual revenue visibility if Oracle can deliver capacity.

rpoconv.note: TTM revenue-to-RPO fell sharply as backlog growth outran recognized revenue.

oci.note: Cloud infrastructure growth accelerated hard, supporting the AI-cloud bull case.

capex.note: Capex intensity is extreme, front-loading balance-sheet and return risk.

fcf.note: FCF is deeply negative as AI datacenter spending overwhelms operating cash flow.

debt.note: FY26 debt financing surged, making funding and leverage a core part of the thesis.

ORCL.summary: RPO and OCI growth are extraordinary, but capex, negative FCF and new financing keep execution risk front and center.

azure.note: Azure growth remains the cleanest proof that AI demand is converting to revenue.

airunrate.note: AI annual run-rate more than doubled, reinforcing Microsoft as a scaled AI monetizer.

capex.note: Capex is rising much faster than revenue, so ROIC is now the main debate.

fcf.note: FCF remains healthy but is compressing as AI infrastructure spend steps up.

gm.note: Cloud gross margin keeps sliding as AI depreciation and usage mix weigh.

MSFT.summary: Azure and AI revenue remain very strong, but capex and cloud-margin dilution are the key offsets.

deposits.note: Monthly deposits eased from April but still imply solid asset-gathering momentum.

options.note: Options trading activity accelerated, supporting high-margin transaction revenue.

crypto.note: Crypto volume improved sequentially, but app crypto remains weak year over year.

gold.note: Gold subscribers hit a record, improving recurring revenue quality.

arpu.note: ARPU is rising, showing better monetization per funded customer.

HOOD.summary: Robinhood still has strong customer asset momentum, with May options and deposits supporting the high-beta bull case.

gm.note: Gross margin is still falling, with tariffs and reset costs delaying recovery.

inv.note: Inventory is finally lower, but the improvement is not yet enough to fix margins.

markdown.note: Promotional pressure remains a drag on the turnaround and full-price mix.

china.note: China remains a major growth drag and limits near-term multiple recovery.

dtc.note: Direct sales are still shrinking as Nike rebalances the marketplace.

NKE.summary: Nike remains in reset mode: inventory is slightly better, but China, Direct and margins are still under pressure.

backlog.note: Backlog keeps compounding, giving strong multi-year revenue visibility.

turbine.note: Gas backlog plus slot reservations jumped, underscoring scarce capacity.

gw.note: Power GW commitments are expanding quickly as demand for firm power rises.

dcpower.note: Datacenter equipment orders already exceeded all of last year.

fcf.note: FCF surged on working capital and EBITDA, though the margin is unusually high.

grid.note: Electrification backlog is rising fast as grid equipment demand stays tight.

GEV.summary: GE Vernova remains a power-demand leader, with backlog, gas slots and grid orders all moving sharply higher.
